title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a programmatic heading. It follows pages that set up a dictionary between geometric data and group-theoretic data. The setting is a situation (X, D, J) over Q: a variety X, a divisor D with components D_i that has been removed, and a set J of marked or tangential 'points'. The open part X' = X \ D has a geometric fundamental group pi_1(X'). This sits in an extension 1 -> pi_1(X') -> E' -> G' -> Gamma (with G' a group mapping to Gamma), where Gamma = Gal(Qbar/Q). The previous page lists structure maps: Phi into Hom(T(Qbar), pi_1) for inertia 'tori', and Psi_j into Splitt(E'_j / G'_j), the splittings (sections) attached to the points j in J. All are equivariant under E' acting by twisted conjugation. The next page restricts to an open subgroup Gamma' (a number field K) and describes the outer action of gamma on finite étale covers via pi_1-bitorsors B_gamma: E -> B_gamma wedge_{pi_1} E.

This page states the programme of a 'gruppentheoretisches Gleichnis', a group-theoretic parable or analogue of the (arithmetic) algebraic geometry of curves in characteristic 0. It has two parts.
(a) Give a complete group-theoretic description of Gamma = Gal(Qbar/Q).
(b) Give a complete description, in typical cases (X, D, J), of all the structure elements listed earlier.
The margin adds that one should in particular recover X from the group-theoretic data via qualitative results. This is the anabelian reconstruction problem.

The NB makes three points.
1. The structure for (X, D, J) automatically induces the same kind of structure for every finite étale cover of X'; this functoriality should be made explicit carefully.
2. One should also make explicit, in typical cases, the 'bouchage de trous' (filling holes). This means adding back some removed components D_i. Group-theoretically it is the quotient of pi_1 by the normal subgroup generated by the corresponding inertia.
3. One should likewise treat the 'forage de trous' (drilling holes) when dim X = 1. This means removing some points of J from the curve. Group-theoretically it means passing from pi_1(X') with sections/points to pi_1(X' minus points).
In modern terms, (a) is the problem behind the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. (b) and the margin form the anabelian programme: reconstruction plus a dictionary of points, sections, inertia and cusps. 'Forage de trous' is the cuspidalization problem: reconstructing the fundamental group of the curve with extra punctures at given (rational or tangential) points from that of the original curve plus a section.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page is a programme statement. The only caveat is the dimension restriction 'si dim X = 1', which Grothendieck himself notes. For higher dimension, removing points does not change pi_1, so 'drilling' only makes sense in that form for curves; this is consistent with the text.

ideas.what: Programme of a complete group-theoretic description of Gal(Qbar/Q), framed as a 'group-theoretic parable' of arithmetic geometry of curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme 1984; letter to Faltings 1983); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984); letter to Faltings (27 June 1983)

ideas.what: Reconstruct X from its (arithmetic) fundamental group data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; proved by Nakamura, Tamagawa (1997), Mochizuki (1999)

ideas.what: Functoriality of the structure under finite étale covers of X'
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility with open subgroups / covers in anabelian reconstruction

ideas.what: 'Bouchage de trous': filling back removed divisor components D_i, i.e. quotient of pi_1 by the inertia subgroups
'Forage de trous' (dim 1): removing points of J (points/sections) and describing pi_1 of the further-punctured curve group-theoretically
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki ('Absolute anabelian cuspidalizations of proper hyperbolic curves', 2007), Hoshi, Hoshi–Mochizuki

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly lists, as part of the anabelian programme, the group-theoretic description of 'drilling holes' at the marked points of a curve. This is the cuspidalization problem, alongside hole-filling, and it is tied to the sections/points J. In the literature this problem is usually presented as arising in Mochizuki's and Hoshi's work in the 2000s rather than as part of Grothendieck's original programme.
missed.quote: expliciter également dans les cas typiques les fameux "bouchage de trous" (en rajoutant certains des D_i qu'on avait enlevés) ou "forage de trous" si dim X=1 (en enlevant certains des ξ∈J)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution: it shows the cuspidalization problem (and its link with the section conjecture via points/sections) was envisaged by Grothendieck around 1980–81. The word 'fameux' suggests he had already thought about it at length.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a restatement of the known anabelian / Galois-group programme. The mildly notable detail is the explicit pairing of 'bouchage de trous' with 'forage de trous', which anticipates the cuspidalization problem usually credited to later work. The page is only a programmatic mention.
transcription_corrections: 'bandages de tores' should read 'bouchage de trous' (filling holes).
'fusion de tores' should read 'forage de trous' (drilling holes).
'(en enlevant certains des J' ⊂ J)' should read approximately '(en enlevant certains des ξ ∈ J)'.
The insertion 'si dim X=1' sits above the last line and qualifies 'forage de trous'.
Margin reads approximately: 'On doit en particulier ... retrouver X ... par résultats qualitatifs ...' (reconstruction of X); the exact wording is uncertain.
'associés pour (X, D, J)' is more likely 'énumérés pour (X, D, J)'; the transcription itself has 'énumérés' a few lines above.
